messages:
jordan: Quick heads-up — ran a set of Monte Carlo sims for the Evo app traffic pattern this weekend. Median tokens/sec stays same but the 95th jumps ~1.8x for a 6h window saturday night. Need ideas on prewarm + batching mix to avoid 99th pct latency spikes.

sophia: Can you paste the sim config/results?

jordan: Pasting minimal snippet and 95/99 numbers.
```
sim: weekend_surge_v3
traffic: 2.0x peak for 6h (22:00-04:00 region-local)
concurrency_dist: empirical from last month
model: gpt-like-13b-quant
hw: p4d-style GPU
results:
 tokens/sec median: 42k
 tokens/sec 95th: 74k
 99th latency: 280ms -> 620ms under current batch config
 gpu-hours extra: +18h per weekend (est)
```

liam: That's a nasty tail. If we prewarm N warm pods, what's the diminishing return? Any sim with warm_pool?

jordan: Yep — ran warm_pool sweeps. Quick summary: +20 warm pods reduces 99th from 620ms -> 360ms but adds ~12 GPU-hours. +40 warm pods -> 320ms but cost +22 GPU-hours.

marta: Region notes: this is APAC-heavy surge. We only have limited spare capacity in ap-south-1; we'd need cross-region reroute otherwise. Reroute adds ~50ms network penalty but reduces prewarm cost since EU/NA spare pool can serve.

sophia: Tradeoff: pay +22 GPU-hrs (approx $1,000/wk) vs cross-region latency +50ms affecting SLAs. Which is worse for product?

liam: We should quantify as cost-per-latency-drop. If +40 pods buys 300ms less tail, that's ~3.3 GPU-hours per 10ms saved in 99th. Not linear but useful. Also consider reducing batch size for that window to cut queueing latency — batch shrink gave 30-40% 99th improvement in microbenchmarks.

jordan: I tried dynamic batch policy in sim: when concurrent_reqs > 1.2x baseline, reduce batch_size by 25% and enable more aggressive KV cache sharing. Outcome: 99th -> 420ms, extra GPU-hours ~+10. So cheaper than full prewarm.

oncall: @jordan @sophia if we go dynamic-batch we need a fast rollback plan. Past incidents show config flaps can spike error rates. Add circuit breaker with fail-open to current config.

jordan: Good call — added fallback rule in the sim: if error_rate > 0.5% within 5min, revert. No sim errors but we should stage it.

marta: Ops constraints: autoscaler in apac has 12m cooldown. Prewarm needs to be scheduled earlier or use reserved warm-pool instances. If we rely on autoscaler, we'll miss first 30min of surge.

sophia: Could we schedule a cheap prewarm window using Dedicated spare capacity? e.g., borrow 30 pods from dedicated pool for the weekend burst and pay transfer fee. Might be cheaper than pushing warm pods across regions.

liam: Quick cost calc: borrow 30 dedicated pods -> ~16 GPU-hrs extra (we pay committed discount rate) -> ~+$600/week. Cross-region reroute (eg EU->APAC) taxes egress + latency impact -> ~$200/week egress + 50ms latency. Prewarm full in APAC -> ~$1k/week. So the cheapest is cross-region, but has SLA hit. Middle ground is borrow Dedicated for weekend.

jordan: Proposal: implement dynamic-batch policy + staged warm-pool (10 pods in APAC) + plan to borrow up to 30 dedicated pods if tail over threshold at 30m. Will create rollout plan and canary config.

oncall: Please tag me when you post the canary plan. Also add alert: 99th latency > 450ms for 10m -> page oncall and trigger borrow flow.

deploy-bot: Canary config created: /canaries/evo-weekend-surge-186500. Schedule: deploy Friday 18:00 UTC -> canary window 6h Saturday 20:00-02:00 UTC.

jordan: I'll open a runbook PR with the exact steps, cost numbers, and rollback. Dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.test/evo/throughput?sim=weekend_surge_v3 (internal).

liam: One more ask: let's add a simulation that assumes model-quantization variance (different kernel perf) — we saw a 12% perf delta between q4f16 builds in prod. That could change GPU-hour calc.

sophia: On it — I’ll run the q-var sweep and post numbers tomorrow.

marta: Thanks team. Ping me if we need to prebook cloud capacity in apac early — that lead time can be 48h for some SKUs. :calendar: 

jordan: Thanks — I'll follow up with the runbook PR and the canary id.
